summary: An API sync is only useful if it lands in the domain tables the read commands query. The list endpoint returns id, title, owner, and timestamps only, so sync-api must follow it with a per-note detail stage that requests the transcript and writes meetings, attendees, calendar events, summaries, folder and space membership, and transcript segments through the same schema path the cache sync uses. Two contracts a regen must preserve: row ownership — every row carries a row_source marker and each sync path deletes only the rows it owns, so the cache and API paths never destroy each other's data (the column is row_source, not source, because transcript_segments.source already means the audio source); and speaker-vocabulary normalization — the API's speaker source enum is microphone/speaker while the store and talktime read microphone/system, so an unnormalized write makes talk time silently report zero seconds for the far end.
reason: The generated sync wrote list rows into the generic resources table, which no read command consumes, so a successful sync still left every meeting, attendee, and transcript command empty. The row-ownership and vocabulary rules are the two places where a correct-looking write silently corrupts or zeroes user-visible output rather than failing loudly.
